first_pass.one_liner: Stripe offers a comprehensive REST API for payments/billing, authenticated via secret/restricted API keys for direct account access, and a full OAuth2 flow (Stripe Connect) for platforms to connect multiple end-users' Stripe accounts.

second_pass.one_liner: Stripe offers a broad REST API (payments, customers, invoices, subscriptions, etc.) authenticated via API keys for single-account use, plus a self-serve Connect OAuth flow that lets platforms instantly get a client_id and let end-users connect their own Stripe accounts.

first_pass.one_liner: Salesforce offers a mature, extensively documented REST/SOAP/Bulk API platform with OAuth2 Connected Apps enabling multi-tenant, self-serve API integrations.

second_pass.one_liner: Salesforce exposes a broad set of official REST/SOAP/Bulk/Metadata APIs authenticated via OAuth 2.0 Connected Apps (or newer External Client Apps), which any developer can self-serve create using a free Developer Edition org—no approval needed unless you want AppExchange marketplace listing/ISV partner status.
second_pass.main_blocker: Salesforce is transitioning Connected Apps to "External Client Apps" with new mandatory OAuth security controls (deadline May 2026), and doc pages are inconsistent/thin on multi-tenant setup specifics, but the underlying OAuth2 Connected App / External Client App flow remains free and self-serve for any developer with a Developer Edition org; only AppExchange marketplace distribution requires a separate paid/partner security review.

first_pass.one_liner: Amazon Selling Partner API (SP-API) offers a broad REST API for seller/vendor operations (orders, listings, inventory, pricing, reports) using LWA OAuth2, but multi-tenant ('public') apps require Amazon approval as a registered public developer, agreement to Solution Provider Portal Agreement/AUP/DPP, security review, and (per policy) listing on the Selling Partner Appstore with a 3-4 week app review.
first_pass.main_blocker: To let multiple end-users (sellers/vendors) connect their own Amazon accounts via OAuth, a developer must register as a 'Public Developer', pass Amazon's application/security review, sign the Solution Provider Portal Agreement, and per policy list the app on the Selling Partner Appstore, which undergoes its own content/compliance review and 3-4 week publication process. Private/self-authorized apps (personal single-account use) are easy and self-serve, but that path does not support other users connecting their own accounts, so it does not satisfy Composio's multi-tenant requirement.

second_pass.one_liner: Amazon SP-API lets sellers/vendors integrate order, inventory, catalog, reports, and finance data via a broad REST API secured with Login-with-Amazon OAuth2, but building a multi-tenant (public) app requires becoming an approved Solution Provider and listing in the Selling Partner Appstore.
second_pass.main_blocker: To let other sellers connect their own accounts (multi-tenant), you must register as a "Public Developer," accept the Solution Provider Portal Agreement/Acceptable Use & Data Protection policies, and get Amazon to review and approve your app (including a functional/security review, 5-day SLA, and additional business-verification + data-security review for any restricted/PII roles) before listing it in the Selling Partner Appstore. A private-app path exists but is capped at 10 self-authorized connections for a single org, which is not viable for a multi-tenant Composio toolkit.

first_pass.one_liner: Otter.ai offers a REST Public API (Bearer token, Enterprise-only workspaces) plus an official OAuth-based, read-only remote MCP server (mcp.otter.ai) for meeting transcripts/summaries/action items.
first_pass.main_blocker: The REST Public API (channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, workspace) is gated to Enterprise workspaces only — the Developer tab/API key creation is not visible to standard accounts and requires an Otter account manager to enable it, so a Composio toolkit built on the REST API would require each end-customer to already be on an Enterprise plan and have API access manually enabled by Otter (admin-approval, not self-serve). Also, auth is per-user API keys (max 2 per user) rather than a public multi-tenant OAuth app, which limits scalable multi-tenant onboarding. Separately, Otter does publish an official read-only MCP server (OAuth-authenticated, available on all plans including free) at https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp, which is more broadly self-serve but only exposes read-only meeting search/summary/action-item retrieval, not the full CRUD surface of the REST API.

second_pass.one_liner: Otter.ai offers a REST "Public/Connect API" (Bearer API-key auth) and an official OAuth-authenticated MCP Server for meeting transcript search, but both are gated to Enterprise-tier customers and require contacting an Otter account manager to enable access.
